original_value: Due to the rapid development of computer technologies, many traditional contents have been digitized, adding to the immensity of digital contents. Through the Internet, various digital contents can be accessed and spread all over the world within the snap of a finger. However, such amazing swiftness and convenience have also brought various kinds of data security, privacy and copyright protection issues. Digital rights management (DRM) systems are access control technologies used to restrict the use, modification, and distribution of protected digital contents. The success of a DRM system relies heavily on a good user authentication mechanism, and user identity verification through biometric information check is a great idea in that the biological characteristics are unique to each user and that such a mechanism releases the user of the trouble of keeping the login info safe from being stolen or mistaken or forgotten. On the other hand, in response to modern people’s prevalent use of mobile devices, DRM systems should also support mobile digital content access. In this paper, we shall propose a novel biometric-based authentication and anonymity scheme for DRM system. To develop our new scheme, we have carefully studied Jung et al.'s scheme, a biometric-based protocol whose architecture is similar to that of a DRM system but not quite the same, and modified it to fit the requirements of a DRM system environment. Our correctness check, security analysis, and performance evaluation have proved the superiority of our new scheme over related schemes.DOI: http://dx.doi.org/10.5755/j01.itc.47.2.18506

result.paraphrase: Rapid advances in computer technology have digitized much traditional content, greatly expanding the volume of digital materials. Thanks to the Internet, digital content can be accessed and shared worldwide almost instantly. Yet this speed and convenience have also created numerous data security, privacy, and copyright protection challenges. Digital rights management (DRM) systems are access-control technologies that limit the use, modification, and distribution of protected digital content. The effectiveness of a DRM system depends largely on a strong user authentication mechanism, and verifying user identity with biometric information is appealing because biological traits are unique to each person and it spares users the burden of protecting login credentials from theft, confusion, or forgetfulness. At the same time, given the widespread use of mobile devices today, DRM systems must also support mobile access to digital content. In this paper, we propose a new biometric-based authentication and anonymity scheme for DRM systems. To create it, we carefully examined Jung et al.’s biometric-based protocol, whose structure is similar to but not identical with that of a DRM system, and adapted it to meet the requirements of a DRM environment. Correctness verification, security analysis, and performance evaluation show that our scheme outperforms related approaches. DOI: http://dx.doi.org/10.5755/j01.itc.47.2.18506
